title: Peru Presidential Election Winner

eventMetadata.context_description: Partial results from Peru's April 12-13 presidential election, extended due to ballot shortages and technical failures affecting over 60,000 voters, show Keiko Fujimori leading with 16.95% at 54.75% of votes counted, ahead of Rafael López Aliaga at 14.40%, positioning both as frontrunners for the June 7 runoff under the two-round system requiring over 50% to win outright. Pre-election polls in early April reflected this tight contest between the right-wing candidates amid a fragmented 35-candidate field, with Fujimori gaining late momentum from her Fuerza Popular base and prior runoff experience, while López Aliaga's Renovación Popular appeal to conservatives sustains his viability. Traders price Fujimori's edge on urban tallies and name recognition, though rural votes and second-round dynamics remain key uncertainties. Roberto Sánchez Palomino trails at 8.12%, buoyed by left-leaning support but unlikely for top-two.

eventMetadata.context_description: Péter Magyar's Tisza party secured a landslide two-thirds majority in Hungary's April 12 parliamentary election, prompting Viktor Orbán's concession after 16 years as prime minister and driving trader consensus to near-certainty on Magyar's ascension. Record turnout underscored public demand for change amid economic woes and Orbán-era fatigue, vaulting the centre-right, pro-EU leader to dominance in a proportional representation system favoring clear mandates. With National Assembly confirmation and a targeted May 5 government handover imminent, markets reflect minimal procedural risk. Realistic challenges—such as Fidesz legal appeals, recounts, or presidential delays—face steep barriers given the supermajority and historical smooth transitions.

eventMetadata.context_description: Mercedes' superior W17 car under 2026's new active aero and power unit regulations has propelled George Russell and Kimi Antonelli to the top of trader consensus, with Russell at 44.5% and Antonelli at 30.6% implied probabilities for the Drivers' Championship. The intra-team duel intensifies as team principal Toto Wolff permits racing without contact, but traders favor the more experienced Russell's racecraft over the 19-year-old's rookie momentum, amid Mercedes' 45-point Constructors' lead. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc trails at 6.3% despite third place on 49 points.
